public_body: Gloucester Community Arts Charter School Board Of Trustees
overall: The AG found the Charter School Board violated the Open Meeting Law by convening a non-emergency 'emergency' meeting and by posting the Saturday notice late, but found no intentional violation and ordered compliance steps.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board improperly convened a Saturday meeting as an 'emergency' after its regular notice was posted too late.
allegations.key_passage: Emergency meetings are reserved for circumstances that are unanticipated and require an immediate response to, for example, protect public safety or health.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Saturday meeting notice was posted after the 48-hour deadline, so the meeting was not properly noticed.
allegations.key_passage: The GCACS Board therefore missed the posting deadline when it posted the meeting at 10:21 a.m., ten hours after the deadline to post a Saturday meeting had passed.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board knew the posting was defective yet convened an 'emergency' meeting anyway, misleadingly.
allegations.key_passage: Nevertheless, because the Board's failure to timely post for the Saturday, November 20 meeting appears, at least in part, to have resulted from confusion about whether or

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25 and the Open Meeting Law regulations, 940 CMR 29.00 et. seq.
Inclusion of the date and time meeting notices are posted on the face of the notice as required by 940 CMR 29.03(1)(b)
Review by all GCACS Board members of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§18-25; the Open Meeting Law regulations, 940 CMR 29.00 et. seq.; and the Attorney General's Guide to the Open Meeting Law
Written certification by each individual GCACS Board Member that have received, read and agree to abide by the terms of this order
